perf_tips:
Autres conseils pour réduire la latence :
• Utilisez un réseau Wi-Fi dédié en 5 GHz ou 6 GHz (avec le casque comme seul client et le PC relié par câble Ethernet)
• Onglet Diffusion : privilégiez l'encodeur matériel (vaapi/nvenc) plutôt que le x264
• Le H.265/AV1 à 80–120 Mbit/s offre généralement une meilleure fluidité que le H.264 à très haut débit
• L'encodage fovéal réduit le temps d'encodage ; 50 % constitue un bon point de départ
• Réglez le profil d'alimentation de votre GPU sur "Performances" pendant que vous jouez.
killcmd_desc: Le bouton Tuer l'app du tableau de bord met déjà fin à tous les programmes lancés au démarrage de manière standard (SIGTERM → SIGKILL). Cependant, certaines applications ignorent cette procédure : les applications Electron (comme VRCX) se ramifient en plusieurs processus, certains AppImages s'exécutent sous un nom de processus différent et quelques outils nécessitent une commande spécifique pour être fermés. Ajoutez ces cas particuliers ici : ils sont exécutés en complément de la procédure d'arrêt normale, juste avant celle-ci.
killcmd_warn: ⚠ Ces commandes sont exécutées dans un shell ; ne saisissez que des commandes en lesquelles vous avez confiance. Les entrées manquantes sont simplement ignorées.
mic_desc: Depuis Proton 11 les microphones virtuels ne sont plus transmis correctement aux jeux. Si vous acheminez de l'audio vers VRChat via un microphone virtuel (par exemple, en utilisant PipeWire pour envoyer Spotify ou YouTube Music dans le jeu), sélectionnez la source d'enregistrement ici et définissez-la comme source par défaut du système. La fonction Réinitialiser rétablit la source qui était active auparavant.

ubuntu_guide_text:
WiVRn ne figure pas dans les dépôts Ubuntu/Debian ; il est donc nécessaire de le compiler une fois à partir du code source.

Une compilation native est plus légère et plus performante qu'une version isolée (en bac à sable) : elle communique directement avec votre GPU et vos périphériques USB, sans la surcharge liée à l'isolation.

Cliquez sur "Copier les commandes", collez-les dans un terminal et laissez le processus s'exécuter (10 à 20 minutes). Ensuite, redémarrez yakuda-connect et tout fonctionnera normalement.

Vous disposerez alors des éléments suivants :
  • wivrn-server dans votre PATH
  • OpenComposite dans /opt/opencomposite (pour VRChat et d'autres jeux OpenVR)

fedora_copr_text:
{name} n'est PAS dans les dépots Fedora officiels — il n'est disponible que sur le dépôt COPR '{copr}'. Les COPR sont des dépôts communautaires qui ne sont pas examinés par Fedora ; c'est pourquoi nous demandons d'abord l'autorisation.

Choisir 'Oui' ouvrira un terminal qui lancera

    sudo dnf copr enable -y {copr}
    sudo dnf install -y {name}

l'un après l'autre. Tout ce que vous avez à faire est entrer votre mot de passe sudo — rien à copier.

Remarque : OpenComposite provient des dépôts officiels et fonctionne parfaitement avec VRChat. {name} est facultatif et offre de meilleures performances dans de nombreux jeux.

Attention : le paquet "envision-xrizer" n'est PAS xrizer ; il contient uniquement des dépendances de compilation pour Envision.

openxr_desc:
Corrige l'erreur "invalid Elf handle" de Steam/pressure-vessel en générant un fichier d'exécution OpenXR valide (avec des chemins absolus vers les bibliothèques WiVRn). Cliquez sur le bouton ; votre fichier précédent est automatiquement sauvegardé. Astuce : ajoutez également cette option de lancement Steam :
XR_RUNTIME_JSON=$HOME/.config/openxr/1/active_runtime.json PRESSURE_VESSEL_IMPORT_OPENXR_1_RUNTIMES=1 %command%
openxr_manual_hint: Si la correction automatique échoue (problème de permissions), effectuez l'opération manuellement : ouvrez le fichier ci-dessous et remplacez-en tout le contenu.

Réessayer avec les droits d'administrateur ? Une demande de mot de passe s'affichera ; ensuite, la propriété du dossier sera transférée à votre utilisateur afin que les modifications ultérieures puissent s'effectuer sans droits root.

oxr_doc_text:
Un ou plusieurs manifestes d'environnement d'exécution OpenXR sur ce système pointent vers une bibliothèque inexistante ou dont l'architecture est incorrecte (32 ou 64 bits).

Steam lit chacun de ces fichiers au démarrage, au sein de son conteneur. Une entrée erronée provoque le plantage en boucle de steamwebhelper avec l'erreur "invalid `Elf' handle" ; Steam refuse alors de démarrer.

{items}

Réparer maintenant ? Les fichiers concernés sont d'abord sauvegardés avec un horodatage ; les chemins sont corrigés lorsque cela est possible, sinon le fichier est désactivé (renommé avec l'extension .disabled). Des droits d'administrateur pourraient être requis.
oxr_doc_nopath: → le manifest n'a pas de library_path.
oxr_doc_done:
Fichiers du runtime OpenXR réparés. Steam devrait redémarrer normalement.

exit_group_desc:
Decides what happens to the WiVRn server when yakuda-connect ends.

On (default): the server is stopped exactly like switching it off on the dashboard — including autostart programs and custom kill commands. This applies to every way of ending the app: the window's X, closing from the taskbar, ending it in a task manager/resource monitor, and pkill.

A hard kill (kill -9, "Kill process", a crash) is covered as well: while the server runs, a small helper process (yakuda-guard) watches and cleans up if the app suddenly disappears.

Off: the server keeps running after closing, as it did up to v1.2.9.
exit_stop_server_tip: On by default. When yakuda-connect closes (also via taskbar, task manager or pkill), the server is stopped like switching it off on the dashboard.

Change the Proton version of a game:

2. Properties… → Compatibility

games_fix_video_tip: About VRCVideoCacher — helps when YouTube videos won't play in worlds.
games_fix_check_tip:
Checks Proton version, launch options, system clock, VRChat's Tools folder and the

games_video_fix_text:
YouTube videos not playing in worlds?

Typical in-game message:
“Loading failed. File not found, codec not supported, video resolution too high or insufficient system resources.”

The URL usually resolves fine — only playback fails, because YouTube ties the address to the client that requested it. When the video player then fetches it itself, the server rejects it.

VRCVideoCacher fixes this by downloading the video itself and serving it to VRChat locally. It replaces VRChat's yt-dlp on startup and restores it on exit.

Check these first — they're free:
• System clock in sync? If the clock is off, the signed video URLs are already expired. The “Video Player Check” covers this.
• RTSP Proton selected? Without the MediaFoundation patches AVPro plays almost nothing on Linux.

About the Google account: You only need the browser extension — and therefore a Google account — against YouTube's bot detection (“Sign in to confirm you're not a bot”). For the error described here it is not required, so try VRCVideoCacher without cookies first. If you do need it, the developers explicitly recommend a secondary account rather than your main one.

Linux setup: requires dotnet-runtime-10.0. By default VRCVideoCacher downloads its own binaries, so there's nothing else to do.

adv_mode_tip: Shows technical details for actions that change something on your system: affected files, required permissions and the matching terminal command to copy. Nothing is executed automatically, and no feature behaves differently — only the extra information appears.
adv_perm_home: write access in your home directory
adv_perm_root_maybe: root via pkexec only if the file belongs to root
adv_fw_explain: Adds a rule to the firewall that is active on this system ({fw}) so the headset can reach the WiVRn server: port {port} TCP and UDP for the connection itself, port {mdns} UDP (mDNS) so the headset can find the PC in the first place. The ports are opened for wivrn-server, not for yakuda-connect.
adv_fw_no_firewall_cmd: # no active firewall found — nothing needs to be opened
adv_oxr_explain: Writes active_runtime.json with absolute paths to the WiVRn libraries. The previous file is kept as .bak with a timestamp.
adv_rt_explain: Points active_runtime.json at WiVRn or at SteamVR. When switching to SteamVR the OpenVR compatibility in WiVRn's config.json is set to disabled and the previous value is remembered for switching back.
adv_prio_explain: Grants the wivrn-server binary the CAP_SYS_NICE capability so reprojection can run at high priority. This is a capability on one file — not a permanently elevated process. It has to be re-applied after a WiVRn update.
adv_wayvr_explain: Downloads the design by cubee-cb from GitHub and copies it to ~/.config/wayvr. The existing folder is backed up beforehand.
adv_osc_explain: Sets one key in the config file of each supported program ({keys}). All other keys stay untouched, and files that do not exist yet are not created.
adv_backup_explain: Copies the current VR configuration into a folder inside your home directory. Reads system folders, but changes nothing outside your home directory.
adv_restore_explain: Copies the backup back. This is the only action that also writes to /usr and /opt — that part runs via pkexec and creates a timestamped backup first. Nothing is deleted; existing files are moved aside.
adv_server_explain: Starts the wivrn-server process as your user and stops it again. Its output goes to a log file in your cache folder.
adv_update_explain: About 1.5 seconds after start, yakuda-connect reads one file from GitHub and compares the version number in it with the installed one. Nothing is sent along except the request itself — no identifier, no system information.
adv_diag_explain: The log is written locally and never sent anywhere. It is only passed on if you copy or save it yourself.
firewall_info:
Open WiVRn ports

Port 9757 (TCP and UDP) carries the connection between the WiVRn server on this PC and the VR headset. Port 5353 (UDP, mDNS) is what lets the headset find the PC — without it the server list in the headset stays empty even when 9757 is open.

The ports are opened for wivrn-server. yakuda-connect itself does not listen on any port. They are not used for telemetry, analytics or data collection.

Only the firewall that is actually active on this system is changed (firewalld or ufw). nftables and iptables are detected but never modified automatically — you get the commands to copy.
streaming_enc_auto: WiVRn picks automatically: nvenc on Nvidia, otherwise vaapi, otherwise x264.
streaming_enc_nvenc: Nvidia hardware encoding — for Nvidia GPUs.
streaming_enc_vaapi: Hardware encoding — for AMD and Intel GPUs.
streaming_enc_vulkan: Vulkan video encode — works on any GPU that supports it. Marked experimental by WiVRn, and only h264/h265, no AV1.
streaming_enc_x264: Software encoding on the CPU — works everywhere, but costs the most CPU and only does h264. A fallback when no hardware encoder works.
streaming_encoder_tip:
Which chip compresses the video stream.

• nvenc — Nvidia GPUs
• vaapi — AMD and Intel GPUs
• Vulkan — any GPU with Vulkan video encode (experimental)
• x264 — software encoding on the CPU

Auto leaves the choice to WiVRn and is the right setting for almost everyone. Picking an encoder your GPU does not have stops the server from starting.
design_desc: Pick a theme, recolour anything you like, or drop an image behind the window.
design_hint: A theme recolours the whole interface. Green and yellow stay as they are on purpose — they mean "running" and "attention".
apt_ppa_title: Install WiVRn from the LVRA PPA?
apt_ppa_text:
WiVRn is not in the official Ubuntu sources; it lives in the Linux VR Adventures project's PPA:

    {ppa}

A PPA is a third-party repository. It stays active after the installation and will also supply updates for WiVRn.

Choosing 'Yes' opens a terminal that adds the PPA, refreshes the package lists and installs WiVRn, one after the other. All you do there is enter your sudo password.

Note: Steam games additionally need xrizer, which the PPA does not carry — it is fetched straight from the GitHub release instead (no repository, no root).
apt_ppa_yes: Yes, add the PPA and install
install_apt_missing: ⚠ Not installed: {pkgs}. Check apt's output in the terminal — usually the PPA has no build for this Ubuntu release.
apt_ppa_unsupported_title: PPA has no build for this Ubuntu release
apt_ppa_unsupported_text:
The PPA {ppa} carries no packages for "{codename}" — the base of this distribution.

Adding it would fail with "Cannot add PPA: This PPA does not support {codename}", so it isn't attempted.

WiVRn is available as a Flatpak from Flathub instead. It runs on any distribution and ships xrizer and OpenComposite with it, so no extra download is needed.

Worth knowing: the Flatpak runs in a sandbox. SteamVR lighthouse trackers don't work with it, the configuration lives under ~/.var/app/, and controlling the server from yakuda-connect is limited.
apt_flatpak_missing:
Flatpak is not installed on this system.

    sudo apt install flatpak

Then try again.
native_guide_text:
On Debian, Ubuntu and Linux Mint, yakuda-connect does not automate the native route — there are too many differences per release: the PPA does not build for every Ubuntu version, an OpenVR translation layer is missing there anyway, and OpenComposite would have to be built by hand.

The guide walks through the native installation step by step.

Afterwards there is nothing else to do here: as soon as wivrn-server is in your PATH, yakuda-connect picks it up on its own, no matter where it came from.
games_manual_note: Not distributed through the AUR or ProtonPlus — the button downloads the build from the GitHub release, verifies its SHA-512 checksum and extracts it into compatibilitytools.d.
games_manual_restart_steam:
{tool} has been extracted into compatibilitytools.d.

Please restart Steam — only then will the version show up in the compatibility settings and can be applied with “Use”.
games_toggle_proton_use_wayland_tip: Puts PROTON_USE_WAYLAND=1 in front of the launch command, switching on the native Wayland path instead of running through XWayland. Only has an effect on Proton builds that carry the WineWayland patches (e.g. Proton-RTSP-Wayland-GE) — other builds ignore the variable. Note: on the Wayland path Xalia is off and Steam Input defaults to off.
autostart_apps_tip: Lists every program installed through the Tools tab.
autostart_apps_hint: Programs and OSC apps installed on this system. Picking one puts its launch command into the row (double-click applies directly).
autostart_apps_none: No program from the Tools tab is installed yet. Install one there first, or type the command by hand.
tools_filter_empty: Nothing matches the search and filters. Clear the search box or set category/status back to “All”.
netbuffers_info:
Enlarge the UDP buffers for WiVRn

WiVRn pushes the video over UDP. If the kernel's socket buffer is smaller than a frame, the kernel drops packets before WiVRn ever sees them — which shows up as stutter, blocky artefacts or short dropouts, especially at high bitrate and resolution.

The target is 25 MiB (26214400 bytes), the value named in the WiVRn documentation. Only net.core.rmem_max and net.core.wmem_max are changed. The *_default values are left alone — those apply to every socket on the system, not just the video stream.

Asks for your password once (pkexec).
netbuffers_ask_text:
Current: {current}
Target:  {target} bytes (25 MiB) for both

How long should this apply?

• Permanently — creates {path} and sets the values right away. Survives a reboot.
• This session only — sets the values right away, writes no file. Back to the old values after a reboot.

Either way you are asked for your password once.
netbuffers_ok_session:
Network buffers set to {target} bytes.

This only lasts until the next reboot. If it helped, press the button again and choose “Permanently”.
netbuffers_fail_text:
Setting them automatically did not work ({err}).

Over Wi-Fi the PC cannot initiate the connection — there you press "Connect" inside the headset.
dashboard_connect_tip_noserver: The WiVRn server is not running. Start the server above first.

apk_choose_folder: Choose a folder for the APK

apk_status_no_release: Error: no release with an APK found (network or GitHub rate limit?).

apk_no_match_server: ⚠ No release matches server {server} — downloading {tag} instead. Client and server must match or the headset will not connect. For git builds the matching APK lives at github.com/WiVRn/WiVRn-APK.

The headset could not match the connection to any app.

Every known WiVRn package name was tried, plus the URL scheme route — so WiVRn really does seem to be missing.

Install it via "Download & install APK" in the Installation tab, or from your headset's store.
adb_fix_tip: Restarts the adb server. Needed after android-tools was updated: /usr/bin/adb is new, but the running server is still the old one.
adb_fix_confirm:
The adb server will be stopped and started again.

Running adb connections will drop, including those of other programs such as SideQuest. The headset may ask for "Allow USB debugging" again afterwards — best to put it on.

Continue?
adb_fix_confirm_udev:
adb reports missing permissions, so the udev rules need to be reloaded.

This will ask for your password. The adb server is restarted afterwards; running adb connections will drop.

Continue?
adb_fix_ok: ✔ adb is talking to the headset again.
adb_fix_failed: The handshake is still not working.
adb_fix_step_restart_failed: The adb server would not start — is another program holding it (SideQuest, Android Studio), or is it running as a different user (started via sudo)?
adb_fix_step_udev_failed: The udev rules could not be reloaded (password prompt cancelled?).
adb_fix_step_install: adb is not installed — add android-tools from the Tools tab.
adb_fix_step_confirm: The headset is asking now: put it on and tap "Allow". Ticking "Always allow from this computer" avoids the prompt next time.
adb_fix_step_still_broken: adb still does not see the headset. Replug the cable (ideally a different port), unlock the headset and check USB debugging in the developer settings.
usb_state_after_update: — android-tools has been updated since the last working access ({old} → {new}); restarting the adb server usually fixes this.
usb_state_mtp_busy: — an MTP session is also open (file manager); close that window, some headsets do not allow MTP and adb at the same time.
usb_connect_ok_generic: ✔ Connection started — put the headset on.
usb_connect_waiting: Waiting for the PICO... If it stays stuck: on the headset, switch the USB option briefly to "Charge only" and back to "File transfer" — that resets the interface.
usb_connect_probably: ✔ The start command went out — the headset should connect now. (adb did not report back, which is normal on the PICO.)
usb_connect_timeout_short: The headset is not answering adb.
usb_connect_timeout:
The headset did not answer adb within the waiting time.

On a PICO 4 this is almost always the USB interface stuck in file transfer mode. How to fix it:

1. Put the headset on
2. Open the USB options
3. Switch briefly to "Charge only"
4. Switch straight back to "File transfer"

Then press Connect again — the attempt keeps running for 90 seconds and takes hold as soon as the headset responds.

If that does not help: close any open MTP window in the file manager and replug the cable.
diag_report_copied:
Diagnostics report copied ({lines} lines).

Contains versions, distribution, GPU, OpenXR runtime, adb and firewall state — no log, no IP addresses, paths shortened.
usb_auto_connecting: Headset detected on the cable — connecting automatically...
streaming_usb_autoconnect_self: Yakuda Connect does this itself: as soon as the headset is detected on the cable and the server is running, it connects automatically — no running WiVRn dashboard needed.
